faq.headline: Questions, answered.
faq.a1: MEWS and Apaleo today, plus Gmail for the inbox — each connected in a few minutes. More integrations are on the way; tell us what you run.
faq.q2: Do I have to switch systems?
faq.a2: No. Fondas sits on top of the tools you already use. Nothing to migrate and nothing for your team to relearn.
faq.a3: About an afternoon. Connect your PMS and inbox, and your first brief can arrive the very next morning.
faq.q4: Does Fondas ever email guests without me?
faq.a4: Never automatically. Every reply is drafted for your review — sending is always your decision.
faq.q5: Where does our guest data live?
faq.a5: In our EU-hosted database, in your own isolated space. Fondas does store the reservation and guest data it reads from your PMS and inbox — that is what the briefs, drafts and answers are built from. It is encrypted at rest, protected by row-level security so one property can never see another's, used only to run your hotel, and deleted when you leave.
faq.q6: Is guest data used to train AI models?
faq.a6: No. Your guests' information is used only to run your hotel's briefs, drafts and answers — never to train shared models.
faq.a7: One flat price per property, per month — everything included, with no per-seat fees. Fondas is in private beta: we onboard a few hotels at a time. Get in touch and we'll get you set up.

trustPage.metaDescription: What Fondas reads, what it stores, where it is hosted, what it never does, and what happens to your data the day you leave.
trustPage.heading: How we handle your data
trustPage.lead: {brand} reads the bookings in your PMS and the mail in your hotel's inbox. This page says exactly what we read, what we store, where it is hosted and what happens the day you leave. Written to be read without a lawyer; the full privacy policy is linked at the end.
trustPage.readsBody: Only what it takes to write your morning brief, your drafts and the answers about your hotel.
trustPage.readsB1: From your PMS: bookings, arrivals and departures, occupancy, rates and the guest profiles attached to them. Through the official MEWS and Apaleo APIs, read-only.
trustPage.readsB2: From your inbox: the messages in the mailbox you connect, contents included, so we can sort them and draft the reply.
trustPage.readsB3: From your account: your name, your work email and the hotel's settings — rooms, timezone, language and the hour you want the brief.
trustPage.storesBody: We store it, and we say so plainly because it is the part some people skip. The seven o'clock brief and the drafts do not come out of thin air: they are written from bookings and emails held in our database. Without storing them there is no brief.
trustPage.storesB1: The bookings and guest profiles we sync from your PMS.
trustPage.storesB2: The guest emails we read and the drafts we write, until you send or discard them.
trustPage.storesNote: Each hotel lives in its own space, isolated in the database by row-level security: one property cannot see another's data, not even by accident.
trustPage.whereBody: In the European Union. The database holding your bookings, your guests and your emails sits on European servers and is encrypted at rest.
trustPage.whereBody2: To write the briefs and the drafts we send the data needed to our AI provider, Anthropic, through its commercial API: under those terms it is not used to train its models. That is the only processing that leaves the European Economic Area, and it relies on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses. The full list of providers is in the privacy policy.
trustPage.never1: Write to your PMS. The connection is read-only: {brand} never edits a booking, never changes a rate, never touches a profile.
trustPage.never2: Send an email without someone on your team pressing the button. The draft waits; you decide whether it goes, and you can rewrite it first.
trustPage.never3: Train models on your guests' data — not ours, not anyone's.
trustPage.never4: Sell, rent or share your data with third parties for advertising.
trustPage.never5: Mix one hotel's data with another's.
trustPage.deleteBody: Cancel and we delete your hotel's data: bookings, guest profiles, emails and drafts. Short-term backups expire on their own. Your account and billing records are kept only for as long as the law requires.
trustPage.deleteBody2: You do not have to cancel to cut us off: disconnect the PMS or the mailbox in settings and the credentials are erased that moment. In the same step you can ask for the bookings and profiles already synced to go too.
trustPage.rolesBody: The hotel is the data controller for its guests' data; {brand} is the processor. That is not boilerplate: it means the data is yours, that we process it only to provide the service and on your instructions, and that when a guest exercises their rights, you are the one who answers — with our help.
trustPage.rolesBody2: For your own account data — your name, your work email, your settings — we are the controller.
trustPage.honestTitle: What we do not have yet
trustPage.honestBody: We hold no ISO 27001 and no SOC 2, and we will not imply otherwise. Those certifications come with size, and we are not there. What we can give you today is this page: the exact list of what we read, what we store, where it lives and what we never do. If your process needs more than that, write to us and we will talk.
trustPage.moreBody: The privacy policy sets out the legal bases, the list of providers, international transfers and the rights the GDPR gives you. For any question about data, write to us:

onYourSide.b1: Nothing to migrate, nothing for your team to relearn.
onYourSide.b2: One place, even when each hotel runs a different system.

security.headline: Your team is already using AI. Just not safely.
security.lead: Right now someone on your front desk is pasting a guest's email into a free chatbot to write the reply in English. {brand} gives them the same speed inside your own environment, on your hotel's data.
security.i1Desc: Your guests' data is stored encrypted, on European servers.
security.i2Desc: Used solely to produce your briefs and drafts. Never to train anything.
security.i3Desc: Cancel and it's erased. The hotel is the data controller; {brand} is the processor.

comingSoon.headline: What lands during the pilot.
comingSoon.lead: Written in the future on purpose: it doesn't do these today. Four things in build, landing while your pilot runs.
comingSoon.i1Desc: The revenue dashboard and hotel analytics. First will come a line in the brief when a night is running soft: a signal, not a pricing engine.
comingSoon.i2Desc: Pre-arrival drafts will include your own paid extras with prices: late checkout, breakfast, parking. One late checkout a week pays for {brand}.
comingSoon.i3Desc: Where you'll actually read it at 6:45.
comingSoon.i4Desc: For the hotels that aren't on Gmail.
